0.0.n: This is her family name, placed before her given name.

0.2.n: A respectful title attached after a person's name, regardless of gender.

0.3.n: Marks Reina Ibuka as the person the sentence is about.

0.4.n: This is the name of a city in Japan.

0.5.n: Marks the place where she was born.

0.6.n: The connecting form of 生まれる links her birth to the next event without ending the sentence.

0.8.n: Combines with 卒業 to specify which level of school she finished.

0.9.n: A noun here; 高校卒業 means finishing high school.

0.10.n: Pairs with 同時に to link the timing of graduation and her move.

0.11.n: Together with と, this presents her move as happening immediately upon graduation.

0.12.n: Refers to clothing and accessories as a field of study.

0.13.n: Links 服飾 to 学校, identifying the school's specialty.

0.14.n: Refers to the institution where she intended to study fashion.

0.15.n: Marks 学校 as the destination of 行く; this particle is pronounced え.

0.16.n: The plain form comes before ため to express the purpose of her move.

0.17.n: Following 行く, this explains why she went to Tokyo.

0.18.n: This is the name of Japan's capital, her destination.

0.19.n: Marks Tokyo as her destination; the verb describing her move is left unstated.

1.0.n: A loanword describing the kind of products the company makes or sells.

1.1.n: Combines directly with ランジェリー to identify her employer's business.

1.2.n: Marks the company she joined as an employee; へ is pronounced え.

1.3.n: The plain past form of 就職する describes entering employment before the next event.

1.4.n: Follows a past-form verb to place the next event later; more formal than あと.

1.6.n: A loanword naming the subject she wanted to study.

1.7.n: Links デザイン to 勉強, specifying the subject of study.

1.8.n: A noun that combines with する to describe studying.

1.9.n: With したい, が can mark what someone wants to do, where を is also possible.

1.10.n: したい becomes したくて to connect her desire to study with the move it motivated.

1.11.n: Describes traveling without anyone accompanying her, not her marital status.

1.12.n: This is the country name, followed by the city name パリ.

1.14.n: This is the city name, specifying her destination within France.

1.15.n: Marks Paris as the destination of her journey abroad.

1.16.n: The polite past form of 渡る describes traveling to another country here, rather than simply crossing something.

0.lit: Ms. Reina Ibuka, born in Chichibu, simultaneously with high school graduation, to Tokyo to go to a fashion school.
0.tip: The sentence ends with 東京へ, leaving the movement verb understood: she went or moved to Tokyo.

1.lit: After getting a job at a lingerie company, wanting to study design, she traveled alone to Paris, France.
1.tip: したくて connects what she wanted to do with her reason for going to Paris.
